source.paraphrase: maxURLLength is a configurable safeguard for URL limits, not a required option on every httpBatchLink.

invariants.why: Whether a batch can exceed the deployed server's URL limits depends on its inputs and transport configuration.
invariants.fixHint: Pass maxURLLength (for example 2083) to httpBatchLink so oversized batches split before they hit the URL limit.
invariants.avoid: A transformer or custom headers do not bound URL length. The non-batched httpLink is out of scope for this rule.

relations.why: TRPC-ERR-001 tells procedures to throw a TRPCError, and TS-THROW-001 denies every throw inside an exported function; routers are exported, so following one fix violates the other.
relations.settle: Exclude router files from TS-THROW-001 (for example **/routers/** or **/server/api/**): tRPC turns a thrown TRPCError into the typed failure the client branches on.

source.work: tRPC documentation, error handling with TRPCError
source.paraphrase: Procedures throw TRPCError with a code, never a plain Error, so the client receives a typed failure it can match on.

invariants.why: A plain Error crosses the boundary as an untyped internal failure. The client cannot tell NOT_FOUND from a bug.
invariants.fixHint: Throw new TRPCError({ code: 'NOT_FOUND' }) (or the code the caller should handle) instead of new Error.
invariants.avoid: This rule sees a throw only in a tRPC context: the file imports a module whose specifier contains trpc, or the throw is inside a query, mutation or subscription call on a receiver whose text contains procedure. A throw in an Express handler or a test with neither is not matched. AggregateError and other built-ins are still untyped throws.

source.paraphrase: Middleware may call next() to forward the existing context, or next({ ctx }) to extend or narrow it.

invariants.why: A bare next() is correct for middleware that only observes or authorizes against the existing context.
invariants.fixHint: Return next({ ctx: { ...ctx, user: ctx.user } }) so the narrowed context reaches the procedure.
invariants.avoid: The rule matches a .use chain whose middleware calls bare next(). Middleware that only observes and changes nothing still needs to forward ctx explicitly.

source.paraphrase: A subscription resolves to an observable or an async generator, so the subscribing caller gets a stream it can iterate and unsubscribe from.

invariants.why: A subscription returning a static value or a bare emitter gives the caller no stream contract: no iteration, no cleanup, no backpressure.
invariants.fixHint: Wrap the event source in observable() from @trpc/server/observable, or make the resolver an async generator that yields values.
invariants.avoid: Returning emitter.on(...) directly still fails: the caller needs the observable wrapper. Queries and mutations are out of scope for this rule.

source.paraphrase: isDev decides whether the API returns stack traces; it defaults to process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'.

invariants.why: isDev: true sends server stack traces to every client in production too, exposing file paths and internals.
invariants.fixHint: Remove isDev so tRPC uses the NODE_ENV default, or derive it from an environment check.
invariants.avoid: A quoted key, a context or meta chain before .create, and other options next to it do not change the setting. Test files are not checked. A value read from a variable is not seen.
